facts.claim: Stripe lets businesses create, edit, archive, and delete products and prices.

facts.excerpt:
Flat rate (good-better-best)

Offer your customers a choice of escalating options, like basic, starter, and Enterprise service levels")

Let your customers pick how many seats or licenses they’ll use and bill them for each.

facts.claim: Stripe has a data migration guide for moving customer and payment data onto Stripe.
facts.excerpt: Successfully migrate your customers and their payments data to Stripe.

facts.claim: Stripe says it can only assist certain migrations when the request includes both customer records and associated payment data.
facts.excerpt: For each type of data migration, we can only assist you if your request includes both customer records and the associated payment data.

Its recent strategy appears to be focused on stablecoins and crypto infrastructure — Bridge, Privy, Valora and PartyDAO — as well as on billing and money movement through Metronome, payment processing startup Lemon Squeezy and Orum.

strategy.observation: Stripe’s data migration guidance is narrow: it says it can only assist certain migrations when the request includes both customer records and associated payment data.
strategy.offer_link: If Stripe is publishing migration guidance with specific eligibility conditions, localized developer docs in Japanese, German, and Brazilian Portuguese could help non-English-speaking teams understand those requirements correctly before they open a migration request.
hypotheses: Stripe may have enough developer traffic in Japan, Germany, and Brazil to justify localized docs.
The documentation team may be looking for ways to reduce confusion and support load around migration workflows.
Stripe may want to improve clarity for developers implementing or migrating payments in non-English markets.
strategy.angle: Stripe’s migration guide has a hard condition: assistance only applies when customer records and associated payment data are both included.
strategy.fit_reason: Stripe clearly has developer documentation that could benefit from localization, and the migration guide is a concrete, docs-heavy example. But the facts do not show an explicit localization priority or a stated need in the target languages, so the link is plausible rather than strong.

draft.subject: Migration docs in local languages
draft.body:
Hi — I localize developer documentation into Japanese, German, and Brazilian Portuguese.

Stripe’s migration guide has a pretty specific condition: support only applies when the request includes both customer records and associated payment data. If that section is hard to parse in English, localized wording could help teams check the requirement before they open a request.

Would it help if I sent a sample localized rewrite of that migration section?
